newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Clinics weak on H1 loss, Netcare buy talks.
newsitem.headline: Clinics weak on H1 loss, Netcare buy talks.

text.p: South African healthcare firm Clinic Holdings Ltd slid over 11 percent on Monday morning after the firm announced a half-year loss and that it may soon see a change of control, dealers said.

By 0855 GMT Clinics was the fourth biggest loser by percentage on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, having lost 75 cents to 570 cents. But volumes as yet were tiny with only 4,700 shares changing hands.
Clinics earlier on Monday posted a first half loss of 7.66 million rand from a previous profit of 21.02 million rand for the six months ended March 31.
It also said that talks with Network Healthcare Holdings Ltd were advanced and could see the change of control of Clinics to Netcare.

"Negotiations have reached an advanced stage for the conclusion of certain transactions which inter alia include the acquisition by Clinics of hospitals of Netcare, the recapitalisation of Clinics and the change of control of Clinics to Netcare," the firms said in a brief statement.
They added that the deal was likely to be sealed soon and a further more detailed announcement will be made then.
"Obviously shareholders are not too happy with the outcome of the talks," a dealer said.

But he added that in general the healthcare sector was not viewed as one likely to enjoy much growth in the near future due to controversy surrounding the industry on account of proposed government reforms.

"You really have to look at where the growth is going to come from and under the (Health Minister Nkosazana) Zuma cloud there's not much future in this (health) industry. There are othere areas of investment on the exchange where you'd get better value for money," a dealer said.
Zuma is a regular target of opposition resignation calls.

She spent about 10.5 million rand of European Union funding on a flop Broadway-style AIDS awareness play and recently said AIDS spread faster because poor people could not afford forms of recreation other than sex.
